The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
BrowserReportSerializer's validate_timestamp/validate_age docstrings claim one of age/timestamp must be present, but the code only enforces mutual exclusion, so reports with neither are accepted.

sugestoes.texto: _get_event_stats passes the captured outer `dataset` to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects instead of the `scoped_dataset` parameter. In the dashboard-widget split path _get_event_stats is called with `discover` for errors-only queries (organization_events_stats.py:365), but the helper evaluates the original metrics dataset and returns False, so error upsampling is skipped even when every project is allowlisted. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the helper.

_is_error_focused_query reads the query from `request.GET` instead of the actual `query` string being executed. The dashboard-widget split path rewrites the executed query to errors-only or transactions-only (organization_events_stats.py:362, 405), so the helper evaluates the user's original query and can make the wrong upsampling decision for the query that actually runs. Change the helper to accept the query string and pass the actual `query` from _get_event_stats.

_is_error_focused_query uses a naive substring check (`"event.type:error" in query`), so a negated query like `!event.type:error` matches and incorrectly enables upsampling for a non-error query. Parse the query or at least reject matches preceded by `!`.

_are_all_projects_error_upsampled tests membership with `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`, which is O(N×M) and is invoked on every events-stats call (multiple times in the widget-split path). Convert `allowlist` to a set before the all() check to make it O(N).

WHAT: `_get_event_stats` decides whether to upsample using the outer request `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` that will actually execute the query. WHY: In the `metrics_enhanced` dashboard-widget split path, `scoped_dataset` is switched to `discover` but the captured `dataset` is still a metrics module, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `False` and allowlisted error queries are not upsampled even though they run against `discover`. HOW: pass `scoped_dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` instead of `dataset`.

issues.descricao: The upsampling decision is evaluated against the request's dataset instead of the scoped_dataset actually queried, so in the dashboard discover-split path (metrics dataset) error queries run against discover skip upsampling even when all projects are allowlisted.
issues.textoGolden: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

comentarios.texto: The upsampling decision uses the closure variable `dataset` while the transformed `final_columns` are executed against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard-split path `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (e.g. `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` at lines 351, 365, 406, 423) than the request's `dataset`, so the `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` branch can be evaluated against the wrong dataset and apply/skip `sum(sample_weight)` for a dataset that was never queried. Base the decision on the dataset actually being queried (`scoped_dataset`) so the transform matches the target of the query.

issues.descricao: _is_error_focused_query uses a substring match for `event.type:error` on the request query, so negated or mixed (OR transaction) discover queries are treated as error-only and get the sample_weight sum instead of count().

comentarios.texto: `_is_error_focused_query` decides whether to apply `upsampled_count()` by doing a naive substring search for `event.type:error` in the raw request query. A query that excludes errors (e.g. `!event.type:error`) or the discover-split query `({query}) AND event.type:transaction` still contains the literal `event.type:error`, so the transform is applied to a non-error / transactions query, summing `sample_weight` where it should be a plain `count()` and producing wrong bucket values. It also ignores the actual `query` passed to `_get_event_stats`, so the decision can differ from the query that is really executed. Match on a parsed/negation-aware condition (or pass the resolved query string) instead of a raw substring test.

The substring check treats `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` as error-only queries. For allowlisted projects this rewrites count() to an aggregation over sample_weight even when the Discover query includes transactions, violating the error-only restriction and potentially failing against a transaction-backed query. Determine the event-type restriction from the parsed query rather than the presence of a substring.

Substring matching does not establish that the Discover query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both return True here, causing count() to be replaced with the sample-weight aggregation for non-error or mixed results in allowlisted projects. This contradicts the error-only guard and can produce incorrect counts. Parse the query and establish an error-only restriction (including negation and Boolean structure), or conservatively skip transformation when that restriction cannot be proven.

issues.descricao: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being applied to transaction queries, because the transaction has no sample_weight and upsampled_count() equals count() for it.

comentarios.texto: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events would still pass if upsampling were wrongly applied to transaction queries. The transaction event has no sample_weight, and upsampled_count uses ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so the result is still 1 and 0. Give the transaction a non-default sample rate or weight so an upsampled count would differ from a plain count, or assert that the transform was not applied.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot falsify over-application of upsampling: the stored transaction has no sample_weight so upsampled_count() (sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) returns 1, same as count(). Give the transaction a sample_weight/client_sample_rate that would diverge (e.g. count 10 if upsampled vs 1 if not), or assert via mock that transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling was not called / yAxes were not rewritten.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being wrongly applied to transaction queries. The stored transaction event has no error_sampling context, so sample_weight is null, and upsampled_count = toInt64(sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) evaluates to 1 for it — identical to count(). If _should_apply_sample_weight_transform/_is_error_focused_query were broken so that a discover query with event.type:transaction gets upsampled, the assertion count==1 (and 0 in the empty bucket) would still pass. Add an event with a known non-1 sample_weight (or assert the emitted query uses count() and not upsampled_count) so the test actually fails when the transaction exclusion is bypassed.

issues.descricao: The test factory helper's docstring promises a valid client sample rate but it copies any truthy float-convertible value (negative, >1, strings), unlike production validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling uses `if client_sample_rate: float(...)` with no type/range check, unlike production _derive_client_error_sampling_rate which requires isinstance(int,float) and 0<rate<=1. WHY: string '0.1', bool True, or out-of-range 5.0 get stored as sample_rate in fixtures while production drops them, making upsampling tests diverge from prod. HOW: mirror production validation before assigning sample_rate.

The new docstring says the client sample rate must be 'present and valid', but the implementation only checks truthiness and float conversion. Negative rates, rates greater than 1, and float-convertible non-finite values are all accepted and written to sample_rate. This falsely tells test authors that this helper enforces sample-rate validity. Either document that it merely copies truthy float-convertible values, or validate the supported sample-rate range and finiteness before setting the field.

issues.descricao: With upsampling active, top-events queries pick and order the top N groups by raw count() (selected_columns/orderby are not transformed) while the plotted series use upsampled_count(), so ranking can disagree with the displayed weighted counts.

comentarios.texto: Only timeseries_columns are upsampled while selected_columns and orderby used to select the Top N remain based on raw count(). discover.top_events_timeseries first queries those unchanged selected columns to choose groups, so a group with fewer retained events but a higher weighted count is omitted in favor of a lower-volume group. Apply the weighted-count transformation consistently to Top N selection and its ordering as well as the displayed timeseries.

issues.descricao: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled and its caller take an organization argument that is never read.

comentarios.texto: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes an `organization` argument — also threaded in from the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — but never reads it: the body uses only `project_ids` and the global option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. The declared parameter is dead. Either the allowlist check is meant to be organization-scoped (the body must actually consult `organization`) or the parameter should be removed from both functions; as written the signature advertises an organization-scoped decision the implementation never makes.

issues.descricao: Claims only bare count() is rewritten, so aliased count, eps(), epm(), count_unique() etc. stay un-upsampled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites exact bare `count()` and passes everything else through unchanged. WHY: yAxes like `count() as foo`, `eps()`, `epm()`, `count_unique()`, `count_if()` keep raw counts while should_upsample is true, returning under-counted timeseries. HOW: parse/normalize the function (strip alias, match function name with args) and rewrite all count-equivalent aggs or explicitly fall back to no-upsampling.

issues.descricao: Rewriting count() to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks responses for transformAliasToInputFormat=1: the result column is translated to the rewritten field string while the serializer still reads `count()`.

comentarios.texto: Replacing count() with `upsampled_count() as count` breaks requests using transformAliasToInputFormat=1. QueryBuilder.process_results translates the count alias to the replacement field string, but the endpoint serializer still resolves the original axis as `count()`, so it cannot read the weighted count from the returned rows. Preserve the original public field name in the result mapping when rewriting the internal aggregation.

issues.descricao: upsampled_count truncates the weighted sum with toInt64 instead of rounding, under-counting the estimate by up to one per bucket.

comentarios.texto: `upsampled_count` wraps the sum in `toInt64`, which truncates toward zero: `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` of e.g. 1.5 or 3.33 yields 1 or 3 instead of the nearest integer, systematically under-counting the upsampled estimate (worst when weights are just below an integer). Use a rounding aggregation (e.g. `toInt64(round(sum(...)))`) so the reconstructed count reflects the intended estimate rather than a floored value.

issues.descricao: The 'no project IDs' test case runs with an empty allowlist mock, so it passes via the empty-allowlist branch and does not verify the empty project_ids guard.

comentarios.texto: The 'no project IDs provided' case does not exercise the `if not project_ids: return False` guard. mock_options.get.return_value was set to [] just above (line 48), so removing the project_ids guard still returns False via the `if not allowlist` branch, and this assertion passes either way. Re-mock options.get to return a non-empty allowlist (e.g. self.project_ids) before calling with project_ids=[], so the empty-project guard is actually falsifiable.

issues.descricao: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` checks membership against the allowlist list for each project; converting it to a set would avoid O(N*M) lookups.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Returning true immediately when dateOverrideExist is true skips the busy-time overlap check below. WHY: A host who has a booking inside a date-override window will still be shown as available, because existing busy slots are never evaluated for override-matched slots. HOW: Remove the early return and fall through to the busy.every(...) check so override windows only make slots available when the host is not busy.

WHAT: Both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, so they are identical. WHY: The working-hours check only validates the slot start time and ignores the slot end time, allowing slots that extend past the host's working hours to be marked available. HOW: Compute `end` from `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` so the entire slot is verified against `workingHour.startTime` and `workingHour.endTime`.

WHAT: The condition compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality and is always false. WHY: A full-day date override (start equal to end) will never be detected, so the intended all-day block/availability behavior is silently ignored. HOW: Replace the `===` comparison with `.isSame()`, e.g. `dayjs(...start).isSame(dayjs(...end))`.

WHAT: The slot-start vs override-end boundary uses `.isAfter()`, which is strict. WHY: A slot that starts exactly when the override ends is actually outside the override window, but it is treated as inside and returned as available. HOW: Use `.isSameOrAfter(...)` so slots starting at the override end time are correctly rejected.

Returning true immediately when dateOverrideExist is true bypasses the busy-time overlap check below. A host who has a date override for the day but already has a conflicting booking will still show as available.

Both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, so they are identical. The working-hours boundary check therefore always compares the slot start minute against the working-hour end time, allowing slots that extend past the host's working day.

The condition compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality and is always false. A full-day unavailable override where start equals end will never be detected, so the slot will be incorrectly kept available.

The slot-start vs override-end boundary uses `.isAfter()`, which is strict. A slot that starts exactly when the override ends is treated as unavailable, whereas it should be allowed (consistent with the start boundary using isBefore/isSame).

issues.descricao: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.textoGolden: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.descricao: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.textoGolden: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

comentarios.texto: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.descricao: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

comentarios.texto: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.descricao: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

comentarios.texto: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.descricao: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

comentarios.texto: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.descricao: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

comentarios.texto: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.descricao: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice with different arities; Ruby's last-definition-wins semantics discard the 4-argument version. The existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 passes four positional arguments (path, path, 100, 100, opts), so it will raise ArgumentError and break emoji resizing. Remove the duplicate method and keep only the intended signature.

The downsize loop runs at most five 80%-resize iterations and does not check whether OptimizedImage.downsize succeeded. After five passes a 10 MB file is still ~3.3 MB, so it can remain above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and Upload.create_for will store an oversized file. Verify the downsize result and loop until the file is actually within the configured limit, or reject the upload if it cannot be reduced.

Each OptimizedImage.downsize call shells out to ImageMagick and then runs ImageOptim.optimize_image! synchronously inside the request thread; the loop can invoke this up to five times per upload. Large-image uploads will block Rails workers and degrade throughput under load. Move image reduction to a background job or limit/queue expensive conversions.

The client-side size check now hardcodes 10 MB instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This ignores the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb, allowing larger non-image uploads than configured and capping image uploads even when the site setting is higher. Restore the dynamic site-setting lookup.

API URL downloads now hardcode 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, allowing remote images larger than the configured maximum to be fetched for downsizing. This bypasses the administrator-configured size limit; restore the SiteSetting-based limit.

WHAT: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both the source and destination path, so ImageMagick overwrites the file it is reading. WHY: A failed or partial convert can leave the tempfile truncated or corrupted, and those corrupted bytes are then passed to Upload.create_for. HOW: Write the resized image to a separate Tempfile path and replace the original tempfile only after convert_with returns success.

WHAT: The downsize loop exits after five iterations even when tempfile.size still exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and the controller proceeds to Upload.create_for without a final size check. WHY: Images that cannot be reduced below the configured limit within five attempts are still stored as uploads, defeating the max image size setting. HOW: After the loop, return a file_too_large error if tempfile.size is still greater than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes.

issues.descricao: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.
issues.textoGolden: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined that overrides the existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147. WHY: Ruby uses the last definition, so the effective downsize now only accepts 3-4 args, and the existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) passes 5 args and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing. HOW: Remove the duplicate; keep a single downsize method whose signature matches all callers (the 4-arg uploads_controller call `downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` and the 5-arg ResizeEmoji call), or rename one of them.

`downsize` is defined twice: the original 5-param form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at lines 145-147 and the new 4-param form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the effective signature is now 4 params and the 5-param version is dead code. The pre-existing consumer app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional args, which now raises ArgumentError on every emoji resize. Either update that caller to the new `dimensions` form or remove the redundant override so the old signature keeps working.

`self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class scope (line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-argument version is dead and unreachable. The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 passes 5 arguments and will now raise ArgumentError (expected 3..4). Remove the duplicate definition (keep only the `dimensions`-based one, or convert resize_emoji's call), otherwise emoji resizing breaks.

issues.descricao: The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

comentarios.texto: Hardcoded max size literal 10 * 1024 replaces site-setting-derived max size. Behavioral concern outside assigned class.

The fixed 10 MB client limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing max_attachment_size_kb. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload those valid files through the composer, although UploadValidator still permits them. Apply the new input ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

WHAT: Client check hardcodes maxSizeKB to 10*1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'], losing image vs attachment distinction. WHY: Sites with smaller max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation then fail server-side, and sites with limits >10MB incorrectly block valid uploads with wrong max_size_kb message. HOW: Restore per-type SiteSetting lookup (keep 10MB only as image downsize ceiling).

issues.descricao: The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
issues.textoGolden: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

comentarios.texto: The controller passes the percentage string `"80%"` as the dimensions argument to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but the consumer requires explicit `WxH` geometry: the code this PR deleted built exactly `"#{width}x#{height}"`, and the animated path runs `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which rejects a percentage. Pass an explicit size (e.g. a computed `"WxH"` from the max KB target) so the auto-downsize actually reduces the file, rather than silently no-oping and leaving oversized uploads.

Caller passes "80%" as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the downsize/optimize instruction builders in optimized_image.rb expect explicit "WxH" geometry (interpolated as -resize #{dimensions}\>). A bare percentage does not satisfy that contract and will produce a malformed geometry. Fix the caller to supply WxH dimensions or add explicit percentage handling to the callee.

issues.descricao: Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new auto-downsize call passes a tempfile path whose name has no `.GIF` extension, so `optimize` never selects the animated branch (`method_name += "_animated" if opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) and uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert from[0]` and keeps only the first frame. WHY: Animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through this path have their animation flattened to a single frame even though SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. HOW: Detect the image type from the original filename/content-type rather than the tempfile path (or pass a flag) so the gifsicle animated downsize path is used for GIF inputs.

Passing the multipart tempfile path to downsize prevents animation detection when that path does not end in .gif, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. OptimizedImage.optimize checks the path suffix and otherwise uses convert with input[0], so oversized animated GIF uploads are permanently flattened to their first frame. Preserve the original image extension in the processing path or pass the image format explicitly to select animated processing.

issues.descricao: The comment promises images are reduced to the allowed size, but the loop only tries five 80% reductions with no guarantee of reaching the limit.

comentarios.texto: The comment says large images are "automatically reduced to allowed size", but the loop only resizes by 80% up to 5 attempts (≈0.33× of the original in the best case) and then stops without any check that the result actually meets `max_image_size_kb`. The prose promises a guarantee the code does not provide; either make the loop actually converge to the allowed size or reword the comment to state that the image is only attempted to be reduced.

issues.descricao: The downsize retry loop ignores the false return of a failed conversion and repeats the same failing ImageMagick call up to five times.

comentarios.texto: The retry loop ignores downsize's false return value and retries failed conversions while the file remains oversized. convert_with returns false on converter failure, so an unsupported or malformed oversized image launches the same failing external conversion up to five times per upload without any changed input. Break on a failed downsize result and return an upload error rather than repeating the conversion.

WHAT: Downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and retries up to 5 times unconditionally while checking tempfile.size. WHY: Failed converts (e.g. SVG, invalid 80%> geometry, corrupt image) burn 5 ImageMagick runs then Upload.create_for still runs with oversized/unmodified file and fails validation, wasting CPU and breaking the feature. HOW: Break on false return and handle failure.

issues.descricao: Claims up to five synchronous ImageMagick runs per oversized upload block request threads and enable DoS.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Up to 5 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize + ImageOptim convert runs execute inline in create_upload request cycle for every oversized image. WHY: Blocks the Rails request thread with CPU-intensive shell-outs per upload, enabling easy request-thread exhaustion/DoS with large images. HOW: Move downsizing to background job or enforce single-pass/timeout.

issues.descricao: Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
issues.textoGolden: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

issues.descricao: The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

sugestoes.texto: Global canManage() grants group management to holders of only the VIEW scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() gates top-level group creation on requireManage(), so a principal with only view permission can create groups. Change the fallback to require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, matching UserPermissionsV2 and ClientPermissionsV2.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses Resource.getId() (the generated resource identifier) where it needs Resource.getName() (the group id stored as the resource name). It also passes that generated id into hasPermission(), which calls resourceStore.findByName() and therefore fails to locate the per-group resource. The returned set contains resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, so UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass invalid values into the UserModel.GROUPS query attribute and group-based user search/count returns wrong results. Use groupResource.getName() for both the permission check and the collected result.

Global canManage() treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for management. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage(), which delegates here, so a principal with only an all-groups VIEW permission can create top-level groups. The fallback permission check should require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, not VIEW.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId() as the group identifier. Group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() are named with the group id, while Resource.getId() is the internal resource UUID. The returned set therefore contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, causing UserModel.GROUPS filtering to match no users and causing the per-resource permission check in hasPermission to fall back to the all-groups resource. Use groupResource.getName() to obtain the group id.

issues.descricao: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, so an admin with only view permission on all groups passes manage checks such as group creation.
issues.textoGolden: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

comentarios.texto: The no-arg canManage() returns true when the caller holds only an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`), whereas the per-group canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) requires MANAGE. WHAT: a caller with only the view scope on all groups is treated as having manage rights. WHY: canManage()/requireManage() gate group creation and other manage operations (e.g. GroupsResource.addGroup -> auth.groups().requireManage()), so a read-only viewer of all groups can create/manage groups — privilege escalation. HOW: drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() only returns true for MANAGE, aligning it with canManage(GroupModel): `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70) evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), identical to canView() at line 52, so a caller granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) correctly requires only MANAGE, and AdminPermissionsSchema defines MANAGE as the manage scope for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the two checks disagree. requireManage() therefore succeeds for read-only administrators, letting them create/update/delete groups, add subgroups and map group roles. Drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() checks MANAGE only.

WHAT: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage on VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). WHY: A caller with only view-all-groups permission passes the manage check, allowing group creation/management reserved for manage. HOW: Check only MANAGE, e.g. hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).

issues.descricao: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource id instead of the resource name (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, so per-group view-members grants are not resolved and user filtering gets wrong ids.
issues.textoGolden: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) as group IDs and looks them up via findByName. WHY: Resource names equal group IDs (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()), so findByName(resourceId) misses and the returned set contains unusable IDs, breaking user search/count filtering by group. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() like V1 does (resource.getName().substring prefix / name) for both the hasPermission lookup and the granted set.

findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and granted set, but AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup defines resource name (not UUID) as groupId and hasPermission looks up via findByName(server, groupId). Use groupResource.getName() for both check and granted set, otherwise lookups miss to all-groups fallback and callers receive authz UUIDs instead of group IDs.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses groupResource.getId() for lookup and result collection, but V2 group resources are named with the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and hasPermission does findByName. Use groupResource.getName() in both places to evaluate the correct per-group resource and to return actual group IDs.

issues.descricao: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

comentarios.texto: findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) does not enumerate the specific group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, because that method creates them without setting their type. Consequently, specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are omitted from the group IDs used for user counts and database filtering. Assign the Groups type to specific group resources and ensure the all-Groups resource is not treated as a model group.

issues.descricao: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.

comentarios.texto: The new V2 group permission IDs are passed into a JPA filter that still requires a legacy group.resource.<groupId> authorization resource. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery checks for that prefixed name, whereas AdminPermissionsSchema creates V2 group resources named only with the group ID, so authorized group members are excluded from user searches even with valid group IDs. Update the database filtering path to support V2 resource naming rather than requiring a legacy V1 resource.

issues.descricao: The new Javadoc for requireManageMembers points to canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers.

comentarios.texto: The javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but this method is the require-variant of canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The text was copied from requireManageMembership above it. It should reference canManageMembers so the documented contract matches the method name and behavior.

The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should refer to canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is a different check, so the doc misdescribes the method.

Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers (copy-paste). Fix link to {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} so the contract describes the method it guards.

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a Stream though the method returns a Set.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a 'Stream of IDs', but the method returns Set<String>. Change the @return text to describe a Set of group IDs.
@return says 'Stream of IDs' but method returns Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Fix doc to 'Set of IDs' to match the signature.

The new @return documentation promises a Stream of IDs, but the method declares Set<String> and both implementations return sets. Describe a set of IDs instead, so the documented return contract matches what callers actually receive.

issues.descricao: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission runs a full permission evaluation for every group resource on each user search and count, costing O(groups) policy evaluations per request.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.

Removing the canViewGlobal short-circuit from the subgroup and group listings makes an admin with an all-groups V2 grant run one full authorization evaluation per group in the listing instead of a single check.
GroupPermissionEvaluator.canView() Javadoc promises VIEW/MANAGE permission grants access, but the V1 GroupPermissions implementation only checks admin roles.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: TagDevice now propagates `ErrDeviceLimitReached` from tagDeviceUI, but tagDeviceUI already wrote the deviceID to the local cache before the DB call. WHY: A request rejected for the device limit has its deviceID cached, so the next retry skips the DB entirely and anonymous authentication succeeds, bypassing the configured limit. HOW: Move the cache write after a successful DB operation, or invalidate the cache entry when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice checks `CountDevices` and then performs the insert/update in a separate step, so the limit is not enforced atomically. WHY: Multiple concurrent anonymous requests can all observe `count < deviceLimit` and each insert a new device, allowing the total number of devices to exceed the configured limit. HOW: Enforce the cap atomically, for example inside a transaction with serializable isolation or by using an upsert that conditionally inserts only when the active-device count is below the limit.

WHAT: Authenticate now calls `TagDevice` synchronously in the request path instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with a timeout. WHY: Every anonymous login blocks on a DB count query plus an insert/update; slow or contended DB responses now directly stall anonymous authentication instead of being logged in the background. HOW: Keep non-limit tagging asynchronous, or wrap the synchronous path in a short timeout so that transient DB slowness does not block auth.

WHAT: The previous goroutine that called `TagDevice` had a deferred `recover()` to prevent panics in the tagging path from crashing anonymous authentication; the new synchronous call has no recovery. WHY: A panic inside `TagDevice` or the DB layer will now propagate through `Authenticate` and can abort the request or process instead of being logged and ignored. HOW: Add a deferred `recover()` around the synchronous `TagDevice` call that logs the panic and allows authentication to continue.

updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected()==0, but on MySQL/SQLite a matched row that does not change (same second updated_at, same client_ip and user_agent) also returns 0 rows affected, so an existing device refresh is incorrectly rejected when the device limit is reached. Fix by distinguishing a no-op refresh from a missing device, e.g., check existence separately or use the same INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE / ON CONFLICT upsert path and let the unique constraint decide.

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now constructs anonStore internally from sqlStore and cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, but pkg/server/wire.go still includes anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and a wire.Bind for anonstore.AnonStore. The provider now requires an int64 device_limit that the wire graph does not provide, and its only former consumer no longer uses it, leaving the provider stale and likely causing wire generation to fail. Remove anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and the anonstore.AnonStore binding from the wire sets.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

sugestoes.texto: The authorization check only matches `userId: user.id`, so team-owned credentials (where `userId` is null and ownership is `teamId`) fail the lookup and return "Credential not found or access denied". Existing `deleteCredentialHandler` accepts a `teamId` and routes the query through `teamId` or `userId`; this handler should do the same so team members and admins can delete cache for team calendars.

The handler directly constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`initFromCredentialId()`, which checks the `calendar-cache` feature flag and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when disabled. When the feature is off globally, this still executes a `CalendarCache` `groupBy` query on every connectedCalendars call for no benefit and can expose stale cache status. Use the existing `CalendarCache.init*` factory or gate the query with the feature flag.

The `deleteCacheMutation` only invokes the parent `onSuccess` callback and does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. If the parent `onChanged` does not refetch, the dropdown continues to display the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful deletion. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess`, matching the behavior of `disconnectMutation`.

The script uses `sed -i '' -E`, which is macOS-specific and errors on Linux because GNU sed interprets the empty string after `-i` as the backup-file argument. Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E ...` and remove the backup, or branch on `uname` to keep the script runnable on both platforms.

WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

The HTML detection regex '<[a-z]+[^>]*>' is case-sensitive, so uppercase HTML tags such as
, , or

Make the anchor pattern case-insensitive, e.g., '(?i)</?a[^>]*>'.

issues.descricao: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

comentarios.texto: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. sugestoes.texto: TopicsController#unsubscribe assumes a TopicUser row always exists. When TopicUser.find_by returns nil, calling tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the request crashes before any unsubscribe happens. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row if missing) or guard against nil before mutating.

The action directly assigns and saves notification_level, bypassing TopicUser.change. This leaves notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id stale and skips the MessageBus notification_level_change broadcast that every other notification-level update performs, breaking the established invariant for manual level changes.

The unsubscribe action is registered as a GET route that mutates the user's notification level. Rails CSRF protection only verifies non-GET requests, so a malicious site can embed or tags pointing to /t/.../unsubscribe and force an authenticated user to unsubscribe. Require a signed per-user token for email links or change the web flow to POST with CSRF verification.

The per-topic unsubscribe_url passed to Email::MessageBuilder is a relative path because Topic#unsubscribe_url returns "#{url}/unsubscribe" and Topic#url is relative. Email clients cannot resolve relative URLs in message bodies, so the unsubscribe link in sent emails will be broken. Pass an absolute URL by prepending Discourse.base_url, consistent with how user_preferences_url is built.

TopicsController#unsubscribe creates @topic_view before mutating and saving the TopicUser notification_level. perform_show_response then preloads that stale TopicView into the Ember bootstrap store as topic_#{id}. The client route's PostStream.loadTopicView reads PreloadStore before making an AJAX request, so the unsubscribe page renders the old notification level. Recreate or reload @topic_view after the save before calling perform_show_response.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.
